around.headline: Delivery worker found murdered near Bellandur Lake
around.summary: A delivery worker was found dead near Bellandur Lake in what police are treating as a murder case, with investigation ongoing. If you work late delivery shifts or wait for deliveries in that stretch after dark, stay alert and share your live location with someone you trust.

around.summary: Raids at Taj, Radisson, Lalit and other 5-star hotel kitchens turned up rotten vegetables and expired milk; the health department has now formed 30 special teams to inspect hotels and restaurants citywide. If you're dining out this week, it's worth checking a restaurant's FSSAI hygiene rating before you book.

around.headline: Today is the deadline to verify your name on Bengaluru's voter roll
around.summary: Nearly half of Bengaluru's 1.03 crore registered voters are flagged for possible deletion under the draft SIR electoral roll, and today, August 8, is the last day to verify your details online or at your booth. If you haven't checked your status yet, do it today to avoid being struck off.

around.headline: Karnataka HC cancels ₹5,000 fee imposed on father to visit his son
around.summary: The High Court struck down a family court order that had charged a father ₹5,000 just to visit his 4-year-old son, calling it against the child's welfare. If you're navigating a custody dispute, this ruling is a useful precedent — visitation rights can't be monetised.

around.summary: A new investigation details how subject experts allegedly leaked NEET-UG questions via handwritten chits marked with NCERT paragraph references. If you have a child prepping for medical entrance exams, treat any coaching centre promising 'guaranteed questions' as a red flag.

street_smart.title: A delivery agent hands you your parcel, exposes himself or makes an inappropriate gesture as you sign for it, then quickly walks off. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru incident: a courier was reported for flashing at a housekeeping staffer in a Bengaluru apartment (The Times of India). Recent evergreen and news topics already covered tenant/landlord rights (twice), SIR-related scams (twice), digital-arrest scams, UPI fraud, auto/cab overcharging, fake job offers, two-wheeler theft, medical emergency response, consumer court basics, phone-snatching/CEIR, loan-app harassment, and ATM/card skimming within the last 3 weeks, so this incident-based scenario is used instead of the rotation.
street_smart.situation: You're at your door signing for a delivery when the rider exposes himself or makes an inappropriate gesture, then hurries off before you can react. He's already gone by the time you process what happened. What do you do?

choices.text: Chase him down the street or the stairwell to confront him yourself.
choices.feedback: Risky. You don't know if he's armed, alone, or has accomplices waiting, and a physical confrontation with no ID or witnesses rarely ends well. It also wastes the minutes better spent capturing evidence while it's still fresh.

choices.text: Post about it on social media to warn others, without filing a formal complaint anywhere.
choices.feedback: Risky. A public post might get sympathy, but it doesn't get the platform to deactivate the rider's account or the police to open a case — and if you misremember details under stress, you risk misidentifying someone. Formal reports are what actually trigger action.

choices.text: Feel too embarrassed or unsure if it's 'serious enough,' and let it go without reporting it.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Unreported incidents are exactly why the same rider can repeat this on someone else — platforms only act on verified complaints, and police can only investigate what's on record. Your discomfort about reporting is precisely what lets the pattern continue.

choices.text: Immediately screenshot the order details, rider name and photo from the delivery app, then report it through the app's safety/SOS option and file a police complaint.
choices.feedback: Correct. The delivery app's order record is your strongest evidence — it identifies exactly who was at your door and when. Reporting through the in-app safety option plus a police complaint gives you two separate channels that can actually get the rider's account deactivated and a case registered.

takeaways: Screenshot the rider's name, photo and order ID from the app the moment something feels wrong — this evidence disappears from easy view once the order is marked delivered.

Every major delivery platform (Swiggy, Zomato, Blinkit, Amazon, etc.) has an in-app safety/SOS reporting option that can suspend a rider's account pending investigation — use it, don't just complain to customer support chat.

You can file a police complaint for indecent exposure/outraging modesty under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, or call the Women's helpline 1091 — you don't need to know the rider's real name, the platform can be legally compelled to share it.

quiz.why: Normal Purple Line service on this stretch resumes from 9 am once the planned works finish.

quiz.question: What must Bengaluru voters flagged in the draft SIR electoral roll do by today, August 8?
options: Verify their details to avoid being deleted from the rolls
Pay a re-registration fee at their local BBMP office
Nothing — the deadline was extended to September
quiz.why: Nearly half of Bengaluru's roughly 1.03 crore registered voters were flagged for possible deletion under the draft roll — verifying keeps them on the final list.

quiz.question: According to a new investigation, how did NTA subject experts allegedly leak NEET-UG exam questions?
options: Via handwritten chits marked with NCERT paragraph references
By emailing question papers to coaching centres
Via a WhatsApp group of examiners
quiz.why: The chits reportedly referenced specific NCERT textbook paragraphs, letting recipients match answers without seeing the actual paper.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age required to be eligible for Rajya Sabha membership in India?
quiz.why: The minimum age for the Lok Sabha is lower, at 25 years — the Rajya Sabha's higher threshold reflects its role as the 'council of states'.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up roughly 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
quiz.why: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the atmosphere — nitrogen's abundance is why it's used to fill everything from packaged snacks to tyres.
